We must also check that the list contains every registration, that submissions received through other channels were included, and that importing them did not introduce duplicates.
<v0>스프레드시트와 바이브 코딩은 사용자가 직접 다루는 표현 수단이 무: <v0>Spreadsheets and vibe coding differ in the form of expression users manipulate directly.</v0> Spreadsheet users model a problem with cells and formulas, and a calculation engine follows their references to compute results. 스프레드시트로 만든 것은 남은 자리를 계산하는 모델이다. 운영자는 명단에: The spreadsheet provides a model for calculating remaining places. Organizers can enter registrations into the list, check availability, and compare results as they change capacity. There is still no screen where attendees enter their own names and email addresses, nor a procedure that checks capacity, saves a registration, and confirms completion. Users are still working with the table in front of them.
스프레드시트는 프로그래밍을 일반 사용자가 업무 문제를 직접 모델링하는 활: Spreadsheets expanded programming into an activity in which ordinary users could model their own work-related problems. Barriers to entry fell, but responsibility for verification and maintenance spread across users and organizations. This development continues from grids and formulas to blocks and templates in no-code tools, and then to natural language and AI.
<v0>노코드 툴은 화면 요소와 기능을 선택하고 연결하는 방식으로 프로그: <v0>No-code tools made it possible to build programs by selecting and connecting screen elements and features. Blocks provided units for combining features, while templates offered preassembled screens and workflows as starting points. Writing code became less burdensome, but deciding which features were needed and how they should work remained the creator’s responsibility.</v0>
앞 절에서는 셀과 수식으로 행사 명단에서 남은 자리를 계산했다. 이제 참: The previous section used cells and formulas to calculate remaining places from an event list. Now let us build a screen where attendees enter names and email addresses, together with a procedure for storing that information in the list. We may also need to display the date and venue, send confirmation messages, and restrict further registrations once capacity is reached.
이러한 도구를 코드로 구현하려면 여러 종류의 작업을 연결해야 한다. 정보: Implementing this tool in code requires connecting several kinds of work: creating an information screen, processing inputs, storing data, and exchanging information with other services. An event organizer may know the needed features precisely without knowing how to express them in a programming language.
화면을 표시하고 데이터를 처리하는 프로그램은 도구 내부에서 작동한다. 제: The programs that display screens and process data run inside the tool. Instead of writing those programs line by line, creators specify desired behavior through the tool’s settings. The tool executes the programs according to those settings.
따라서 노코드를 사용하더라도 배워야 할 것은 남는다. 어떤 요소를 선택해: Using no-code tools therefore still requires learning: which elements to select, where entered values are stored, and under which conditions the next action runs. <v0>Less effort goes into learning programming language syntax, while understanding the tool’s structure and the relationships between its features becomes necessary.</v0>
서로 다른 노코드 툴들 속에서도 공통적인 제작 방식을 찾을 수 있다. 필: Different no-code tools share certain ways of building. Users select ready-made units for needed features, configure their values, and define their relationships. Blocks and templates are two concepts that help explain this process.
<v0>블록이란 노코드 툴에서 제작자가 선택하고 설정해 사용할 수 있도록: <v0>A block is a predefined functional unit that creators can select, configure, and use in a no-code tool.</v0> Tools provide software-building capabilities as individual components, and creators select and combine those they need. This article calls these functional units ‘blocks’, although their names and forms differ across tools.
블록이 담당하는 기능은 화면 구성부터 데이터 처리와 동작 제어까지 다양하: Blocks serve functions ranging from screen layout to data processing and control flow. An event registration screen can contain text blocks for the event name, schedule, and venue, input fields for names and email addresses, and a registration button. Looking up list entries, saving new registrations, and branching according to remaining capacity can also be provided as components. Creators build the registration procedure by selecting both visible elements and the actions behind them.
<v0>각 블록에는 도구가 미리 구현한 기능과 제작자가 조정할 수 있는: <v0>Each block combines functionality implemented by the tool with settings the creator can adjust.</v0> For a name field, the creator specifies the displayed label and whether input is required; for an email field, the accepted value type. For saving, they choose the destination list and map input values to its fields. The name field, for example, maps to the list’s ‘Name’ column and the email field to its ‘Email’ column. Rather than writing the saving function’s internal code, the creator connects screen inputs to storage locations.
여러 블록을 조합할 때는 실행할 순서와 조건도 정해야 한다. 신청 버튼을: Combining blocks also requires defining execution order and conditions. Pressing the registration button can trigger input validation, followed by a capacity check and a check for an existing registration from the same email address. If the conditions are met, the tool adds a row and displays confirmation after saving. An already registered address leads to an existing-registration notice; full capacity leads to a registration-closed notice. Depending on the tool, these relationships are expressed with connecting lines or by selecting actions and conditions from lists.
이때 제작자는 각 기능이 받는 값과 다음 단계에 넘길 결과를 이해해야 한: Creators must understand what each feature receives and what it passes to the next step. They need to check that names and email addresses are stored in the correct columns and that confirmation appears after a row is added. <v0>Blocks reduce the work of implementing individual features; creators design the overall structure by selecting, configuring, and connecting them.</v0>
<v0>템플릿이란 노코드 툴에서 특정한 목적에 맞게 여러 구성 요소를 미: <v0>A template is a basic framework in which a no-code tool has arranged and connected components for a particular purpose.</v0> Before creators specify every element and setting individually, the tool provides an assembled starting point. Creators choose a template close to their goal and modify its contents and features to build the result.
템플릿이 포함하는 범위는 도구의 목적에 따라 다르다. 웹사이트 제작 도구: What a template includes depends on the tool’s purpose. A website builder may provide page structures, text and image layouts, colors, and fonts. <v0/> An app builder may also provide data fields, navigation between screens, and actions responding to user input. An automation tool may preconfigure services, actions, and information passed between them. Evaluating a template therefore requires examining its configured features and relationships as well as its appearance.
<v0>블록이 개별 기능을 조합할 단위를 제공한다면, 템플릿은 그 단위들: <v0>Blocks provide units for combining individual features; templates provide assemblies of those units.</v0> Some decisions about required elements, placement, execution order, and conditions have already been made. Working from this structure reduces the burden of planning and configuring everything from scratch. Examining the preassembled elements and their connections also helps creators learn how software is built with that tool.
행사 신청용 템플릿을 골랐다면, 먼저 예시 행사명과 날짜, 장소를 실제: After choosing an event registration template, first replace its sample event name, date, and venue with the actual information. If attendees need to provide names and email addresses, adjust the fields accordingly and adapt the button and confirmation text. Decide whether to retain or remove fields such as party size or affiliation according to operational needs. Whenever fields change, check that their values are still connected to the list and saved correctly.
템플릿을 선택할 때는 미리 정해진 신청 절차를 살펴볼 필요가 있다. 신청: When selecting a template, examine its predefined registration procedure. Immediate confirmation and a requirement for organizer approval need different messages and different recorded statuses. <v0>Templates provide some design and configuration in advance; creators must understand that structure, decide what to keep or change, and adapt it to their purpose.</v0>
<v0>노코드 툴에서는 수정 가능한 초안을 만들고 그 결과를 확인하면서: <v0>No-code tools allow requirements to become more specific through building an editable draft and examining its results.</v0> It is difficult to define every needed feature and usage pattern at the outset. A basic assembly of blocks and templates gives creators actual screens and behavior on which to base decisions about what is needed and what should change.
행사 신청 폼의 초안을 직접 사용해 보면 필요한 조건이 더 구체적으로 드: Trying a draft registration form reveals more precise requirements. Looking at the screen helps determine what should happen when someone submits an empty name or whether the venue should be shown again after registration. An organizer reviewing the list may realize registration order matters and add a field recording the submission time. Problems and missing information discovered through using the draft inform the next revision.
시각적 제작 환경에서는 필요한 변경을 화면 요소나 설정에 바로 반영할 수: In a visual authoring environment, changes can be applied directly to screen elements and settings. Creators can adjust layout and properties, data fields, or conditions for running actions, then inspect the result again. The draft can also provide a shared reference for discussion with users. Users give feedback on concrete screens and behavior, allowing creators to refine requirements and configuration together.
Checking results requires examining both appearance and actual behavior. Even if a screen looks correct, creators must separately verify that data is saved correctly, actions run under the intended conditions, and connected services complete their processing. These checks show how well the draft meets requirements and clarify what the next revision needs.
노코드 툴의 역사는 시각적 프로그래밍, 웹사이트 제작, 데이터 관리, 업: The history of no-code tools comprises several developments with different purposes, including visual programming, website creation, data management, and workflow automation. The examples below show how these developments changed the ways users assemble programs.
정보를 구성하는 기본 단위는 카드이며, 여러 카드는 스택이라는 묶음으로: The card was the basic unit for organizing information, and cards were managed in collections called stacks. Creators distributed information across cards and set links between them to define how users explored it. They could also copy graphics, buttons, and input fields from existing stacks to create new configurations.
화면 구성과 함께 프로그램의 동작을 제어하는 수단도 제공했다. 제작자는: It also provided ways to control program behavior alongside screen layout. Creators could use the scripting language HyperTalk to specify how buttons and cards behaved. Direct placement of screen elements and scripting of detailed behavior took place in one environment.
HyperCard의 의의는 <v0>화면을 이루는 요소와 정보 사이의 연결: HyperCard’s significance was that <v0>creators could directly manipulate the relationships between screen elements and information</v0>. A visible screen layout could become the starting point for building a program with linked information and behavior.
블록은 개별 동작뿐 아니라 사건에 따른 실행, 조건 판단, 반복 등을 표: Blocks express not only individual actions but also event-driven execution, conditions, and repetition. Creators select blocks, configure their values, and connect them to define program behavior. The arrangement and connections show which instructions run in which order and under which conditions.
이 방식에서는 명령어의 철자와 기호를 직접 입력하는 부담이 줄어든다. 제: This reduces the need to type command names and symbols correctly. Creators work with program structure by examining and combining commands presented as blocks. Logical decisions about sequence and conditions are expressed by selecting and connecting visual units.
템플릿을 활용하는 제작 방식에서는 사이트의 목적에 가까운 기본 구성을 선: With templates, work begins by choosing a basic configuration close to the website’s purpose. Creators replace sample text and images, add needed elements, and remove unnecessary ones. The template provides a starting point for examining and changing the page’s overall structure and design. <v0/>
시각적 편집기에서는 화면 요소를 직접 선택해 위치와 크기를 바꿀 수 있다: A visual editor lets creators select screen elements directly and change their positions and sizes. They refine the page while seeing how its elements fit together and can copy existing elements into other areas. Building a website’s screen becomes a process of selecting and manipulating individual elements.
Wix에서는 <v0>미리 구성된 화면을 출발점으로 삼아 웹사이트의 형태와: In Wix, <v0>creators can start from a preassembled screen and directly refine a website’s form and content.</v0> A template supplies the page’s basic structure, while the visual editor adjusts text, images, and layout to suit its purpose. This reduces the burden of designing everything from scratch and lets creators work toward the desired website by inspecting and revising the visible result.
<v0>Bubble은 화면의 구성뿐 아니라 데이터의 구조와 앱의 동작을: <v0>Bubble is an authoring environment for visually configuring not only screens but also data structures and app behavior.</v0> Its official founding account describes data handling and workflow configuration in the early tool being developed in 2012. The goal was to let users build working web apps without writing code themselves. <v1/> (published: 2020-06-26)
데이터를 구성할 때 제작자는 앱에서 어떤 정보를 저장하고 사용할지 정한다: When structuring data, creators decide what information the app stores and uses. They define data types, fields, the format of each field’s values, and relationships between different data. Features that display information or process user input operate on this structure.
A workflow defines which actions run when an event occurs. Creators select actions and conditions, linking operations that store or modify data with subsequent actions. Editor settings thus express relationships between screen elements, stored information, and executable tasks. <v0/>
자동화의 기본 구성은 작업을 시작하는 사건인 ’트리거’와 그 뒤에 실행할: An automation consists of a ‘trigger’, the event that starts it, and ‘actions’ that follow. Creators choose which event in which service starts the automation, then connect the subsequent tasks. Linking several tasks to one starting event creates a processing flow across services.
작업을 연결할 때는 단계 사이에 전달할 정보도 지정한다. 제작자는 앞선: Connecting tasks also requires specifying information passed between stages. Creators decide which values from a preceding stage supply which inputs to the next. Different services may name the same information differently, so values must be understood and mapped to appropriate fields. These configured relationships determine what information passes to subsequent tasks whenever the automation runs.
Zapier의 의의는 <v0>여러 서비스의 기능과 데이터 이동을 하나의: Zapier’s significance is that <v0>features and data transfers across multiple services can be assembled into a single workflow</v0>. Creators use each service’s capabilities while designing what information moves between services and which tasks follow. Zapier applies the no-code approach to service integration and workflow automation.
<v0>소프트웨어가 어떤 조건에서 어떤 결과를 내야 하는지는 제작자가 정: <v0>Creators must define which results the software should produce under which conditions.</v0> For an event form, this includes whether to accept submissions missing a name or email address, what to tell someone registering again from the same address, and what to display after capacity is reached.
같은 행사에 같은 이메일 주소로 들어온 신청 가운데 첫 건만 남기려면,: Keeping only the first registration from each email address for the same event requires checking the existing list before saving. For an address already registered, show an existing-registration notice without adding a row. Add a condition preventing the save step when capacity has been reached as well.
<v0>As features increase, relationships between data and tasks must also be managed.</v0> Adding a remaining-places display and confirmation emails means several features use the same list. The registration count supplies the availability calculation; names and email addresses supply the messages.

Changing only one can leave the screen showing available places while registration is closed. Storing capacity in one field and having related features use it makes changes easier to trace.
입력창과 저장 항목, 작업 흐름에도 역할을 알아볼 수 있는 이름을 붙일: Input fields, stored fields, and workflows also need names that reveal their roles. Being able to trace where ‘Registrant email’ is entered and which message uses it as the recipient helps identify related features to check when changing that field.

Compare availability before and after registration to verify that the screen correctly reflects the saved data.

Decide who can view and modify names and email addresses while building the form.

Alongside designing the registration screen, configure which users can receive the list. <v0/> (section ‘Client-side data’)

Describing features in natural language, running generated programs, inspecting their results, and requesting revisions lowers the effort required to turn an idea into an implementation. This led to testing ideas through prototypes, creating tools for personal needs, and sharing building experiences. These examples do not, however, quantitatively establish the causes of vibe coding’s spread. This section distinguishes reasons people could try it from signs of widening interest. Reducing the burden of code knowledge. Building programs usually requires learning a language’s syntax, a development environment, and libraries. Connecting external services also requires understanding APIs, application programming interfaces through which programs exchange requests and data. For someone unfamiliar with this process, implementing even a simple feature involves learning. A clearly understood problem may remain unaddressed because its implementation is unfamiliar. Natural language requests allow participation before all this knowledge has been acquired. People who understand their field’s needs and what makes a result useful can begin by turning that understanding into requirements. For a webpage searching local support organizations, for example, they can explain the intended users, searchable information, and presentation of results, then try the screen and request missing features. Domain knowledge helps define requirements and judge usefulness. Willison likewise argued that automating a specific personal task should not necessarily require a computer science degree or programming education [14]. Lovable, a service for building web apps through natural language, provides another example of broader participation. Reporting in July 2025 put its active users at 2.3 million and daily project creation above 100,000 [5]. These figures describe one service’s usage, rather than proving that every user was a nondeveloper or demonstrating vibe coding’s effectiveness. They do show a substantial audience for tools that help turn ideas into screens and features. Testing ideas with working prototypes. Reducing implementation time broadens what people can attempt. They can first build a prototype to test essential features, then identify needed functionality and revisions through use. A written proposal can leave people imagining different screen layouts or user journeys. A clickable screen makes missing features and points of friction easier to discuss concretely. If an idea seems unnecessary, they can change direction or try another. Lower initial effort makes such iteration easier. Willison described vibe coding as useful for prototyping to test whether an idea could work [15]. Prototyping and iterative improvement existed in earlier development, but natural language requests can offer people with less experience a way into that process. When building requires considerable time and money, there is a stronger incentive to fix requirements early and minimize changes. When an initial result is easy to obtain, it becomes easier to build first and discover or adjust goals through the resulting behavior. Speed also motivated experienced developers. In March 2025, TechCrunch reported that 25% of startups in Y Combinator’s winter batch had generated approximately 95% of their codebases with AI [6]. This concerns a particular cohort as reported; it is not a measurement of time saved or evidence of the overall performance of vibe coding. Building small tools for personal needs. A clearly felt inconvenience in work or daily life may still be too costly or time-consuming to justify a dedicated program. Lower implementation effort can make these small needs worth addressing directly. A planner can build a screen demonstrating an idea; a student can devise a calculator or visualization for studying. Their activities supply the program’s purpose and criteria for judging results. New York Times reporter Kevin Roose described building an app suggesting packed lunches from refrigerator photos in about ten minutes, connecting it to the idea of software for one person [16]. Linus Torvalds’s audio effects project AudioNoise also illustrates creating a needed supporting tool. He said he wrote the core audio processing code himself while using vibe coding mainly for Python visualization tools to inspect results [13]. From addressing one person’s inconvenience to supporting professional work, the amount delegated to AI can vary with the features and risks involved. One researcher’s experience: building a tool for an experiment. A researcher without a programming degree found checking and saving sensor data during experiments cumbersome. Needing a tool suited to the experiment, the researcher began building one by describing desired features to AI. They requested graphs and file storage for sensor data, ran the program, and reported errors and inconveniences to guide revisions. Performance testing with actual equipment and further development were still needed, but the researcher could envision the needed functions and attempt their implementation. Understanding the experimental process provided the starting point. Turning a domain-specific inconvenience into requirements and improving a result through direct use illustrates why someone might become interested in vibe coding.

When someone publishes their process, prompts, or results, others can adapt them to their own purposes. Articles and videos showing the process encourage experimentation; prompts illustrate how to explain needed information and conditions. A runnable or reproducible result lets newcomers begin by examining existing features and changing some of them. Shared experiences can reduce the next user’s initial effort, and newly shared results can carry applications into other fields. Tool growth also indicates widening interest. In July 2025, Tech.eu reported that Lovable had 2.3 million active users, more than 100,000 projects created daily, and annual recurring revenue of $100 million approximately eight months after launch. ARR annualizes recurring revenue such as subscriptions. These figures describe the service’s usage and revenue at the time of reporting [5]. Interest in the term itself also increased. In March 2025, Willison cited coverage by the New York Times, Ars Technica, and the Guardian, together with online discussion, noting that ‘vibe coding’ was beginning to describe AI-assisted development more broadly [14]. Collins selected it as its word of the year, and Merriam-Webster also explains it in a slang entry [10] [8]. Service usage, news coverage, and dictionary inclusion measure different phenomena. Together they indicate widening interest, but cannot establish how much each factor contributed to the spread. Changing entry barriers gave people reasons to try vibe coding; published building experiences and media introductions made its possibilities more widely known. As participation broadened, so did the work covered by the name. Section 2.4 distinguishes its definitions and scopes of use.

Input length and effective use also differ in recent long-context LLMs. Liu and colleagues changed the position of an answer-bearing document and compared question-answering performance. In a 20-document experiment, GPT-3.5-Turbo achieved 75.8% accuracy when that document came first, 53.8% when tenth, and 63.2% when last. A larger window creates room for longer material but does not find missing evidence or update obsolete information automatically. Reducing input alone does not automatically improve freshness or accuracy either. Current information requires appropriate retrieval and updating, and organizing input must preserve evidence needed for the task. Context engineering addresses both conditions to find an appropriate quantity and arrangement of information for the current task.

The same tool may also run noninteractively through a single command in scripts or automation. Section 6.2 covers retry limits and stopping conditions during repeated execution and verification; 16.3 covers persistent agents triggered by schedules or events.
background agent는 작업을 맡기면 사용자가 지켜보지 않는 곳: A background agent accepts a task, works out of view, and returns a result. GitHub’s Copilot cloud agent, OpenAI’s Codex Cloud, Claude Code cloud sessions, and Cursor Cloud Agents operate this way (<v0/>; <v1/>; <v2/>; <v3/> (all accessed: 2026-10-28)). Users assign work through web interfaces, issue or pull request comments, editors, or terminals. The agent clones the repository into an isolated remote environment, installs dependencies, edits files, and runs tests. It then posts changes to a branch or pull request and reports changes and test results. Meanwhile, users can do other work or delegate several tasks concurrently.
이 형태에서 사람의 일은 작업 전과 작업 후로 몰린다. 작업 전에는 무엇: Human work concentrates before and after execution. Before work begins, people must specify what to do, its boundaries, and what counts as finished. Weak instructions can produce misguided results because redirecting work midstream is harder. Afterward, people review the changes and decide whether to accept them. Remote execution also matters: local-only data and settings are absent, while repository contents and task information move into that environment. Section 6.1 covers completion criteria; Chapter 10 covers verifying returned results; and 15.1 examines how delegating and waiting for several tasks changes individual and team routines.
첫째, 네 형태는 같은 축 위의 네 칸이 아니다. 일반 chat, AI: First, the forms are not four positions on one axis. General chat, AI IDE, and terminal agent describe interaction environments; background agent describes how work proceeds. They can overlap, as when a task assigned in an editor or terminal runs remotely. VS Code Copilot can hand work to a cloud agent, and Claude Code can start cloud sessions from a terminal.
둘째, 네 형태는 발전 단계가 아니다. 표의 아래쪽이 더 앞선 도구라는: Second, these are not stages of development. Lower rows in the table do not imply more advanced tools or the disappearance of forms above them. Just as spreadsheets and no-code tools remain useful after AI coding tools emerge, each form suits particular work and coexists with the others.
셋째, 제품과 형태는 일대일로 대응하지 않는다. Claude Code는: Third, products do not map one-to-one to forms. Claude Code is available through terminals, editor extensions, desktop apps, and the web; Codex through a CLI, editor extension, and cloud service. Cursor offers both in-editor agents and remote Cloud Agents. Product updates can add another form. Asking ‘In which form are we using this tool for this task?’ is more precise than assigning a product one category. Section 17.3 considers whether these forms may converge.
넷째, 터미널에서 동작한다고 자율성이 높은 것은 아니다. terminal: Fourth, terminal operation does not imply high autonomy. A terminal agent can require approval for every edit, while an AI IDE can edit multiple files without it. Settings and human intervention, more than form, determine independent progress. Intervention is examined further among the considerations below.
형태를 고를 때 살펴볼 것은 다섯 가지다. 지금 작업이 어떤 상태인가,: Five considerations guide selection: the task’s current state, what AI must see and change, when people intervene, what they receive for review, and where execution occurs. The first four concern how work proceeds; the last is a prior constraint. These are not scores to add together. They interact, and one can eliminate an option before the others are considered.
설명에는 하나의 작은 작업을 계속 예로 든다. 이미 있는 CSV 분석 스: We use one small hypothetical task throughout: adding missing-value handling and charts to an existing CSV analysis script. Here, we consider only the form in which to delegate it. Section 4.2 covers reproducible data analysis with AI.
Barke 등은 프로그래머 20명이 코드 생성 도구인 GitHub Cop: Barke and colleagues observed 20 programmers solving tasks with GitHub Copilot and identified two modes (<v0>Barke et al., Grounded Copilot: How Programmers Interact with Code-Generating Models</v0> (Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages 7(OOPSLA1), 2023)). In acceleration mode, programmers already know the next step and use the tool to reach its implementation faster. In exploration mode, they do not yet know how to proceed and use outputs to examine possibilities. Their treatment of suggestions differed: acceleration-mode participants quickly scanned for fit and accepted them, finding long multiline suggestions disruptive. Exploration-mode participants compared several suggestions or used them as starting points, inspecting them more closely before acceptance.
이 구분이 형태 선택에 중요한 이유는, 탐색 중인 작업을 실행 중인 작업: This distinction matters because delegating exploration as if implementation were already decided can harden unmade decisions into code. Asking an agent to ‘handle missing values’ before deciding whether to drop or fill them lets it choose and implement either. A working result may then make that choice seem the default. Conversely, conducting a clearly defined implementation entirely through chat wastes time repeatedly copying code, executing it, and reporting results.
그래서 형태를 고르기 전에 지금이 어느 상태인지부터 묻는 편이 좋다. 간: Before selecting a form, identify the current state. A useful signal is whether completion can be described in one sentence. ‘Fill missing values in every numeric column with its mean and print counts before and after treatment’ indicates readiness for execution. If the description cannot go beyond ‘Handle missing values appropriately’, exploration remains necessary. Exploration suits lightweight, disposable outputs; execution suits forms that directly apply and check changes. Barke and colleagues studied a completion-centered tool and did not prescribe particular forms for exploration or acceleration. That connection is this book’s interpretation.
같은 프로젝트에서도 상태는 바뀐다. 처리 방법을 정하는 동안은 탐색이고,: Task state changes within a project. Choosing a treatment method is exploration; applying the chosen method across files is acceleration. Work forms can change accordingly. Section 3.4 discussed preserving exploration decisions as specifications and plans.
AI가 다룰 수 있는 범위는 대략 네 단계로 넓어진다. 대화에 붙여 넣은: AI’s scope expands through roughly four levels: code pasted into a conversation, project files, the local execution environment with commands, tests, and libraries, and external systems such as remote repositories or services. The four forms provide different scopes.
범위가 좁으면 AI는 사용자가 준 정보만으로 판단한다. 사용자가 빠뜨린: With narrow scope, AI judges only supplied information and guesses what is missing: function names defined elsewhere, installed library versions, or actual data-column names. The result may be syntactically correct and plausibly explained but unusable in the project; Section 9.1 covers such errors. Broader scope lets AI locate files and execute code to reduce these mismatches, but also enlarges what it can change. Unrequested changes to files or settings are discussed in 9.2.
그러면 범위는 어디까지 열어야 하는가. 이 책이 제안하는 기준은 AI가: How broad should scope be? This book proposes granting enough for AI to check whether its task is finished. A new chart function may require only a conversational description of inputs and outputs. Integrating missing-value handling with an existing preprocessing module requires access to that module and its callers. Checking results on real data requires execution. Tasks spanning files, requiring execution to verify, or touching external systems are likely to exceed conversation-only work.
사람이 개입하는 방식은 세 수준으로 나눌 수 있다. 매 응답을 보고 다음: Human intervention has three levels: progressing together by reviewing each response before the next request; letting AI proceed but approving every file change or command; and defining scope, delegating, then reviewing the finished result. General chat, AI IDEs, and terminal agents mainly use the first two; background agents are closer to the third. As noted, a terminal agent can move between the second and third depending on approval settings.
개입이 줄어든다고 사람의 판단이 줄어드는 것은 아니다. 판단이 일어나는: Less intervention does not mean less human judgment; judgment shifts from during the task to before and after it. Working together allows immediate redirection. Delegating and waiting requires clearer scope and completion criteria beforehand and consolidated review afterward. Reducing intervention is therefore closer to postponing review. This is the book’s proposal, rather than a research finding.
함께 진행하는 쪽이 나은 경우는 진행 중에 방향이 바뀔 가능성이 클 때,: Working together is preferable when direction may change, changes are difficult to reverse, or criteria for correctness cannot be determined before seeing results. Refining chart axes and colors by looking at the chart is faster with immediate feedback than delegated waiting. Applying an already defined missing-value rule consistently across several scripts can instead be scoped, delegated, and reviewed afterward. Section 6.2 covers retry limits and stopping conditions.
네 형태가 돌려주는 것은 점점 많아진다. 일반 chat은 설명과 코드 조: The four forms return progressively more material: general chat offers explanations and snippets; an AI IDE, file diffs; a terminal agent, diffs and execution records; a background agent, a branch or pull request with a change summary and test results. These outputs provide evidence for judging completion. Selecting a form therefore requires asking both what AI can produce and whether you can verify it.
두 질문을 나누어야 한다는 점은 초기 연구에서도 드러났다. Vaithil: Early research illustrated the need to separate these questions. Vaithilingam and colleagues had 24 participants complete programming tasks with and without GitHub Copilot (<v0>Vaithilingam et al., Expectation vs. Experience: Evaluating the Usability of Code Generation Tools Powered by Large Language Models</v0> (CHI 2022 Extended Abstracts)). Copilot did not necessarily improve completion time or success, yet most participants wanted it for everyday programming because it provided useful starting points and reduced online searching. They also struggled to understand, edit, and debug generated code, substantially obstructing task completion. This study concerned an early tool, not current product performance. Its distinction between producing code and enabling human review remains relevant.
돌려받는 결과물이 많아지면 검토가 쉬워지기도 하고 어려워지기도 한다. 실: More returned material can make review easier or harder. Execution records and test results reveal what was checked without requiring line-by-line reading. But changes spanning several files and dozens of command records require deciding what to inspect first. What matters is what the material lets you judge, rather than its volume.
여기서 가장 흔한 함정은 끝났다는 보고와 끝났다는 증거를 혼동하는 일이다: A common trap is confusing a completion report with evidence of completion. ‘Missing-value handling is complete’ does not reveal which rules affected which columns, how row counts changed, or whether anything was actually executed. Reviewable results require specifying what should accompany the response: applied rules, missing-value counts before and after treatment, commands and their outputs, and anything not checked. The last item matters particularly. Section 9.1 discusses plausible but false output. Section 10.3 covers agents changing code merely to pass tests, misrepresenting their behavior, and using work records to verify what happened.
이 고려사항에서 형태 선택의 한 가지 조건이 나온다. 맡기고 기다리는 형: This yields a condition for delegated, out-of-view work: you must be able to define completion in advance and have a way to verify the result, such as tests or an executable checking procedure. If either is missing, working together while inspecting results is preferable. Sections 6.1 and 10.1 cover completion criteria and test design; 10.3 covers reconstructing decisions from agent records; and 12.3 covers controlling returned changes through branches and automated checks.
마지막 고려사항은 AI가 실행하는 코드와 읽는 데이터가 어디에 있는가이다: The final consideration is where the code AI executes and the data it reads reside. Terminal agents run on the user’s computer; background agents run in isolated remote environments, sometimes on an organization’s own servers. Content pasted into general chat and files consulted by AI IDEs also reach a service’s servers whenever the model is externally hosted.
로컬에서 실행하면 내 환경 그대로 결과를 확인할 수 있지만, 에이전트의: Local execution lets you verify results in your actual environment but directly exposes your files and environment to the agent’s actions. Remote isolation separates execution from your computer, keeping the impact of mistakes within that environment. However, the repository and necessary data must move there, and local-only data or settings are unavailable.
이 고려사항은 다른 네 가지보다 먼저 걸리는 경우가 많다. 분석할 CSV: This consideration often precedes the others. If a CSV contains personal information or unpublished research data, first determine whether that data may be supplied to the AI tool before considering convenience. If not, options narrow considerably. You may anonymize it, substitute synthetic data, or need an operating arrangement that sends no data outside. Section 9.5 discusses transmission, training use, and retention conditions; 5.3 covers model and hosting choices; and 17.2 covers operating models yourself.
이 꼭지는 이번 작업을 어떤 형태로 시작할지를 다룬다. 여러 작업을 오래: This section concerns which form to start with for the current task. Section 7.2 discusses establishing an agent environment for longer-term delegation, including session continuity, memory, and permission allocation.
다섯 가지를 따지는 순서에도 일정한 흐름이 있다. 먼저 실행 위치에서 걸: The five considerations suggest a sequence. First check execution-location constraints: restrictions on supplying data may eliminate options immediately. Then identify task state. If still exploring, begin with lightweight, immediately inspectable outputs and make necessary decisions first. Once the task is clear, choose scope and intervention together. Provide enough scope for AI to verify completion, and match intervention to the likelihood of redirection and difficulty of reversal. Finally, check reviewability. Delegated waiting requires both completion criteria and verification means; if either is absent, return to working together.
이 순서는 한 번 정하고 끝나는 절차가 아니다. 같은 결측치 처리 작업도: This is not a one-time procedure. For the same missing-value task, you might explore treatment methods in chat, apply a chosen method to existing code in an editor, move to an execution-capable environment to test real data, and delegate applying the rule across other scripts within a defined scope. As task state changes, choose the form again.
바이브 코딩 주변에서 태어나고 진화하는 개념들의 사전이다. 항목마다 정의: This dictionary records concepts emerging and evolving around vibe coding. Each entry gives a definition, origin, and current status. Because new concepts appear and meanings change, the appendix remains permanently unfinished and is the book’s most frequently updated part. Each entry is a contribution unit. New entries and assignments are managed in the repository’s TOPICS.md.
자연어로 AI 코딩 에이전트에게 지시해 소프트웨어를 만드는 방식이다. 좁: A way of building software by instructing AI coding agents in natural language. Narrowly, it describes iterating by inspecting execution results without directly reading generated code. Broadly, it refers to AI-assisted development in general.
Andrej Karpathy가 2025년 2월 트윗에서 만든 말이다. 원: Andrej Karpathy coined the term in a February 2025 tweet containing ‘fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists’ (<v0>original tweet</v0>). In his first-anniversary retrospective in February 2026, he called it a ‘shower of thoughts throwaway tweet’ (<v1>retrospective tweet</v1>).
2025년 11월 Collins 사전 올해의 단어로 선정되며 일반어가 됐: The term entered general usage and became Collins Dictionary’s word of the year in November 2025 (<v0>announcement</v0>, <v1>report</v1>). Simon Willison proposed distinguishing development without reading code from AI-assisted development overall (<v2>article</v2>), but actual usage mixes the two meanings.
원하는 출력을 얻기 위해 모델에 주는 입력, 즉 프롬프트를 설계하는 기술: The practice of designing the input, or prompt, given to a model to obtain a desired output. It includes discovering and systematizing techniques such as arranging few-shot examples and eliciting chain-of-thought reasoning.
프롬프트 한 줄이 아니라 모델이 보는 컨텍스트 전체, 즉 파일, 문서,: The practice of designing the full context a model sees, including files, documents, conversation history, and tool outputs, rather than one prompt alone. It reflects a shift in the bottleneck from how to phrase a request to what information to show.
Tobi Lütke(Shopify CEO)가 2025년 6월 19일 트윗: Tobi Lütke, Shopify’s CEO, named it in a June 19, 2025 tweet, and Karpathy posted an endorsement (<v0>Karpathy’s tweet</v0>). Simon Willison and Phil Schmid each wrote explanatory articles (<v1/>, <v2/>).
AI가 한 번 답하고 끝나는 것이 아니라 도구를 호출하고 코드를 실행하고: A way of working in which AI does more than answer once: it repeatedly calls tools, executes code, checks results, and chooses subsequent actions. It is the technical form that made vibe coding practicable.
Who first used ‘agentic coding’, and when, requires verification. Anthropic’s ‘Building Effective Agents’ from December 2024 provides a reference explaining the loop structure itself (<v0>link</v0>).
CLI형 코딩 에이전트(Claude Code 등)와 IDE 통합형 에이전: CLI coding agents such as Claude Code and IDE-integrated agents are representative implementations. Sections §2.3 and §8.2 discuss tool history and loop structure, respectively.
Steve Yegge가 바이브 코딩이라는 말이 나오기 전에 만든 용어다: Steve Yegge coined the term before ‘vibe coding’ appeared (<v0>O’Reilly podcast</v0>); its exact earliest use needs verification. Yegge coauthored the book ‘Vibe Coding’ with Gene Kim, but precise publication details also need checking.
바이브 코딩의 속도를 유지하면서도 결과물의 책임을 지는 작업 방식을 가리: A way of retaining vibe coding’s speed while taking responsibility for its results. It is effectively a proposal to reintegrate engineering practices such as verification, testing, and review into vibe coding workflows.
에이전트를 실제로 작동하게 만드는 실행 환경, 즉 도구 접근, 권한, 루: The execution environment that makes an agent operational, encompassing tool access, permissions, loop control, and context management. The formulation ‘Agent = Model + Harness’ expresses the view that harness design influences agent quality independently of model capability.
프롬프트 엔지니어링에서 컨텍스트 엔지니어링을 거쳐 하네스 엔지니어링으로: It has been described as the third stage after prompt engineering and context engineering (<v0>Faros AI blog</v0>). Who first used ‘harness’ for an agent execution environment before that article requires verification.
AI에게 바로 코드를 시키지 않고 먼저 명세, 즉 스펙을 함께 작성한 뒤: A development approach that begins by jointly writing a specification rather than immediately asking AI for code, then uses the specification to guide generation and verification. It is often presented as a response to the verification problem in vibe coding without reading code.
메인 에이전트가 특정 작업을 별도의 독립된 에이전트 인스턴스에 위임하는: A structure in which a main agent delegates a specific task to an independent agent instance, or an individual agent executing such a delegated task. A subagent typically has its own context window and tool-access scope and returns its result to the main agent when finished. Coordinating multiple subagents concurrently or sequentially forms a multi-agent system.
자동화된 시스템의 실행 과정에 사람의 확인이나 개입 지점을 명시적으로 두: A design that explicitly includes human checks or intervention points during automated execution. In AI coding agents, it means mechanisms requiring approval before actions such as file changes, command execution, or deployment that can be difficult to reverse.
언어 모델이 사실이 아니거나 존재하지 않는 내용을 그럴듯하게 생성하는 현: A language model’s generation of plausible content that is false or nonexistent. Typical coding examples include presenting nonexistent functions, libraries, or APIs as real.
품질 검토 없이 대량으로 생성된, 낮은 품질의 AI 산출물을 가리키는 말: Low-quality AI output generated at scale without quality review. ‘Workslop’ refers specifically to outputs colleagues or organizations must consume, such as reports, documents, or code.
AI 코딩 에이전트가 환각으로 만들어낸, 실재하지 않는 패키지명을 공격자: A supply chain attack in which an attacker registers a nonexistent package name hallucinated by an AI coding agent. A developer who installs the agent’s suggestion unchanged instead installs the attacker’s malicious package.
유래 확인 필요. 누가 언제 이 용어를 만들었는지 원 출처를 찾아 검증해: Origin needs verification. Primary sources are needed to identify who coined the term and when. It appears to derive from typosquatting, registering package names that exploit typing mistakes, but that lineage also requires checking.
AI 모델이 외부 도구, 데이터 소스, 서비스와 통신하는 방식을 표준화한: A protocol standardizing communication between AI models and external tools, data sources, and services. Implementing a compliant server allows different AI applications to reuse the same tool-integration code.
코딩 에이전트가 파일 시스템 바깥의 도구(브라우저, 데이터베이스, 사내: It has become a standard route for coding agents to access tools beyond the file system, such as browsers, databases, and internal systems. Some practical implementations are also replacing MCP servers with direct API calls.
모델이 답을 생성하기 전에 외부 문서나 데이터베이스에서 관련 내용을 검색: A technique that retrieves relevant material from external documents or databases and includes it in the prompt before a model answers. It enables responses to incorporate current information or private documents absent from training data.
토큰은 언어 모델이 텍스트를 처리하는 최소 단위로, 단어보다 작을 수도: A token is the smallest unit in which a language model processes text; it may be smaller than a word or span several words. A context window is the maximum number of tokens the model can reference at once.
코딩 에이전트가 다룰 수 있는 코드베이스의 크기, 대화의 길이, 컨텍스트: This limit affects the size of codebases agents can handle, conversation length, and the number of files included in context. Some observers argue that larger windows make context engineering (G3) more important. Section §5.3 covers practical management techniques.
AI 모델이나 에이전트의 출력을 정해진 기준에 따라 채점하는 절차, 또는: A procedure for scoring model or agent outputs against defined criteria, or the test collection used for that scoring. Analogous to software unit tests, evals quantitatively assess performance and regressions.
AI 시스템의 입력과 출력에 제약을 걸어 의도하지 않은 행동이나 위험한: Mechanisms constraining AI inputs and outputs to prevent unintended behavior or dangerous results. They operate at several levels, including prompt filtering, output validation, and execution-permission restrictions.
코딩 에이전트에서는 파일 접근 범위 제한, 위험 명령 차단, 실행 전 승: Coding-agent examples include restricting file access, blocking dangerous commands, and requiring approval before execution, overlapping considerably with human-in-the-loop design (G11). Sections §9.2 and §9.5 discuss security and responsibility, respectively.
